key_insight: SE-RRMs (Symbol-Equivariant Recurrent Reasoning Models) build permutation equivariance into recurrent reasoning architectures so symbol symmetries are handled exactly rather than by expensive data augmentation, yielding more robust and sample-efficient symbolic reasoning.
problem_solved: Neural reasoning models (e.g., for Sudoku, ARC-AGI) struggle with symbol permutations and rely on costly data augmentation; SE-RRMs address symmetry handling directly in the model.
method: Embed permutation equivariance into RRM architectures (HRM / TRM family) so outputs transform consistently under symbol permutation.
Modify recurrent reasoning layers (equivariant mappings / tied weights across symbol permutations) to preserve symbolic structure across iterations.
Train with less augmentation and evaluate on symbolic tasks (e.g., Sudoku, ARC-AGI) to demonstrate improved generalization and efficiency.
impact: Practitioners get smaller, more data-efficient reasoning models that generalize across symbol permutations without heavy augmentation — useful for compact symbolic problem solvers and settings with limited labeled data.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: RRM vs SE-RRM showing equivariant layer that enforces permutation symmetry.
Bar chart: performance/data-augmentation tradeoff comparing baseline RRMs and SE-RRMs (accuracy vs amount of augmentation).
Illustration: example symbolic tasks (Sudoku/ARC) with arrows showing permutations mapped consistently by SE-RRM.
Flowchart: recurrent reasoning loop highlighting equivariant update step and preserved symbol relationships.
paper_authors: Richard Freinschlag, Timo Bertram, Erich Kobler, Andreas Mayr, Günter Klambauer
